messages.subject: Re: χ2/df >3,but CFI,TLI,SRMR are good,how to understand it?how to further develop the model?
parts:
It's hard to get an excellent fit with such a large model, and the
p-value for RMSEA reflects the large sample size--focus on the RMSEA
point estimate in this case because the confidence interval width is
essentially zero.

Most likely the lack of fit you do have is from omitted
cross-loadings, probably small. Frankly, with 60 items, 1700 df and a
simple structure, I'd be quite pleased with what you got.

If you want really to improve your values fits, you can try some of this ideas/options:
  1. Try to exclude some items with loadings below of 0.5 or 0.6. Be careful don't affect the sense and kernel of construct factor.
  2. Get the modification indices of your cfa model with this command: `lavaan::modindices(fit,  sort. = TRUE, maximum.number = 20)` . This output allow you see cross-loadings on items or suggestions of correlations between error variance.
